posts.cooked:
In Oblivaeon games, where do effects live?

I’m talking about things like Legacy’s Galvanize buff, Wraith’s Stun Bolt reducing the damage a target can do, or Void Guard Dr. Medico’s Immunization.

The way it was explained to me, they “live” in the play area of the player, character, or target that created the effect, even if that thing moves Battle Zones. That doesn’t seem like a big deal, but it can do weird things when you’re switching Battle Zones 

Case in point, if VG Dr. Medico uses Immunization in Battle Zone 1, and all other players take damage, but then Dr. Medico is incapacitated and the new hero moves to Battle Zone 2, the Immunized heroes won’t be immune to damage until they also move to Battle Zone 2 at some point before that player’s next turn.

Or, if Wraith uses Stun Bolt on Oblivaeon, but then moves to the other Battle Zone, Oblivaeon won’t do less damage unless Oblivaeon and Wraith are in the same Battle Zone again. So, if Wraith is going to Stun Bolt the big guy, she also has to stay with him or her stunning effect goes away with her… unless they come back in contact, then it restarts.

The fact that the effects always travel with the origin and never with the recipient is what makes this weird. I don’t imagine that Wraith is carefully removing her Stun Bolts when she leaves the area, then asking for a time out if they come within reach before the beginning of her next turn. The Immunization shots Dr. M distributes don’t seem like they would only work when you’re around him.

For now, I’ll play it this way, but it’s a rule that doesn’t seem to make sense as it currently stands.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I agree.

In a normal villain fight, if Legacy uses Galvanize and is knocked out, the Galvanize doesn't immediately wear off. It lasts on the other heroes until the start of his turn. Whereas, if he plays Inspiring Presence and is knocked out, or the card is destroyed, the effect wears off immediately because the card providing it is no longer in play. Same thing with Wraith's Stun Bolt: the damage debuff on whatever target she hit doesn't go away because she or her card are suddenly no longer in the game.

This has set up a clear precedent on how ongoing effects work in Sentinels that absolutely makes no sense with Oblivaeon as currently implemented in the digital game, for the reasons you state here. I could see an effect like Galvanize moving away from a battle zone with Legacy, maybe, but not something like Stun Bolt or Syncopated Onslaught, where the effect is applied to a target for a set duration. But it's one of those things I can live with, I suppose, it's probably not going to trip me up that often.

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: You have to keep in mind that each battle one is like playing two different games.  The source of affects stay with that hero.  So if a hero leaves a Battlezone that affect no longer affects anything in that Battlezone.  If they carry an affect like Galvanize it then applies to the new Battlezone they are part of.  I realize it can come across as odd but I think it keeps things a bit simpler as to whether you need to track an affect in a Battlezone or not.

posts.cooked:
The rule is written in the rulebook, and the digital version follows it: "Cards and effects in one battle zone cannot affect or be affected by anything in the other battle zone, unless there is game text that says otherwise."

It's not inconsistent at all with classic/team games, which you can consider as taking place in a single battle zone.

If Stun Bolt is in the first battle zone, its effect works on targets there, even if the Wraith is incapacitated, just like a classic/team game. It cannot affect targets in the other battle zone, just like in a classic/team game it can't affect targets in a whole other game of Sentinels.

I understand you may feel there's a thematic disconnect, but the mechanics are fairly straightforward and come from that single rule in the rulebook.

posts.name: dennis
posts.cooked:
MigrantP:

The rule is written in the rulebook, and the digital version follows it: “Cards and effects in one battle zone cannot affect or be affected by anything in the other battle zone, unless there is game text that says otherwise.”

That’s not the question. The question is “Where is the Effect?”

Using Stun Bolt to hit a target from Battle Zone 1 to Battle Zone 2 clearly Breaks the rules.

But if I hit something in Battle Zone 1, then Wraith or the target moves to Battle Zone 2, it stops working until they get back together. That’s not what the rule says. The rule says cards and effects can’t affect something in the other battle zone. This is why we need to know where the effects “live”.

If the card is causing the effect, it would go away when the card was removed or Wraith was incapacitated, so the card can’t be where the effect is.

If Wraith is causing the effect, it would go away if she were removed from the game entirely, such as on page 3 of Oblivaeon. I don’t think it does that either. (Haven’t tested this.)

The effect moves with something, since it can be resumed if both targets end up together in the other Battle Zone, so the effect doesn’t exist in a specific Battle Zone.

The only other logical place for the effect to live would be with the target, which would mean it should move with the target between Battle Zones and always be in the same zone as the target. The effect and the target are still in the same zone. It should still work until it’s appropriate expiration.

This is the tabletop forum, and it’s a tabletop question. How do you track this on the table, or was this an accident in design?

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Your question is based on an incorrect assumption (and believe me, most of us held it for a long time before official clarification came through).  Effects do not have locations.  They do not "live" in a place.

If someone uses an untargeted effect with a duration, like Galvanize, it stays with them.  If someone uses a targeted effect with a duration, it functions only as long as the source and the target are in the same zone.  If one of the two moves zones, the effect is suppressed.  I assume, though have not seen clarified, that if the second target then moves to the same zone as the first, the effect resumes.

The weird thing, and the one I'm hung up on, is that a card cannot affect another card if the first card moves to the other battle zone, but it can affect another card if it is removed from the game entirely.  In fact, I believe, and I'm happy to be corrected, if The Wraith uses Stun Bolt on a target and then is removed from the game somehow, and then the other target changes zones, the effect will persist!  And if my assumption above is correct, if The Wraith uses Stun Bolt, then moves to another zone, the effect will stop working, but if The Wraith is then removed from the game, it will start working again.

Thematically nonsensical?  Yes.  Unintuitive?  Yes.  But a logical inference from the way the rules are phrased.
